item_name: Design-partner / 'shape the app' pilot programs in vertical SaaS

market_sizing.target_buyer: Founder/operator at an innovator-segment SMB who is articulate, opinionated, and wants to influence the tool they will use for 5 years. Typically the founder of an indie cosmetics/SPF/coffee/candle brand at AU$300K-$2M revenue who has hit the ceiling of their current tool.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Tactic-precedent count, not segment count. Common Paper data: ~hundreds of US vertical-SaaS companies run formal design-partner programs at any time. AU vertical SaaS running design-partner programs: [uncertain] estimate 30-80 active programs across all verticals. ~50% of YC-style early-stage B2B SaaS use the pattern.
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: hundreds (Common Paper standardised the template); UK: dozens; high precedent in vertical SaaS (Zenoti, Toast, ServiceTitan, Procore all started this way).
market_sizing.typical_size: Design partners themselves: 5-25 FTE brands at AU$500K-$3M revenue — large enough to have real workflow but small enough that the founder can make a buying decision in one meeting.
market_sizing.annual_revenue_band_aud: Design partners typically AU$500K-$3M revenue (sweet spot: enough complexity to stress the product, small enough to commit to a 3-6mo program)
market_sizing.growth_trend: Pattern is becoming standardised. Common Paper's free template (2023) and OpenView writing made it the default vertical-SaaS early motion. Growing usage post-2024 as AI lowers build cost and vertical specificity wins.

fit_and_timing.addressable_window: now — Manuva is at the perfect stage (pre-launch with core shipped, lot tracking landing, accounting + Woo + Amazon connectors as roadmap items design partners can shape)
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: None blocking. Design partner motion works best BEFORE roadmap is fully shipped, because partners shape the priority order. Manuva should commit design partners NOW for Xero/MYOB connector quality, lot tracking field-test, and Woo/Amazon prioritisation.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Free during pilot (3-6mo), then Growth $249 or Pro $499 at 30-50% discount for 12-24 months post-conversion
fit_and_timing.time_to_value_days: 30-60 days to first real production run on the tool; 90-180 days to full reference-quality case study

economics.incumbent_pricing: Best-practice playbook (current): Common Paper free template with 3-6mo term, 43% include future discount, 49% are 3 or 6 months. Equity offered in rare cases (0.25-1%). Most common AU vertical-SaaS structure: 100% free for 3-6mo, then 30-50% off list for 12-24 months, in exchange for feedback + case study + reference call rights.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: Design partners pay $0 during the partnership; their value is reference logo, product feedback, and case study harvest. Post-conversion ACV expected AU$2,400-$5,000/year per partner.
economics.estimated_arpu_aud: 0 during pilot; AU$150-$350 effective ARPU post-conversion at 30-50% discount on Growth/Pro
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 3 — discount unwinds at month 12-24, returning customer to full list; modest expansion from add-ons.
economics.churn_risk: 2 — design partners who shaped the product are the stickiest customers in vertical SaaS. Once they have invested 3-6 months and have BOMs/inventory inside, switching cost is enormous. But high concentration risk: if 1 of 5 partners churns, you lose 20% of cohort.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC near-zero; founder-time CAC very high: ~40-80 hours per partner across 3-6 months (weekly calls, custom feature scoping, hand-holding onboarding). At AU$150/hr notional = AU$6,000-$12,000 in founder time per design partner.
economics.ltv_estimate_aud: Per-partner LTV understated by direct math (AU$3,000/yr × 4yr × 70% margin = AU$8,400). True LTV multiplied by reference value: each strong design-partner case study unlocks 5-15 downstream customers. Effective LTV per partner including reference halo: AU$30,000-$80,000.
economics.ltv_cac_ratio: 3-7 : 1 once reference halo is counted; 1:1 to 1.4:1 if counted naively
economics.multi_channel_count: 1-3 channels typical (most early design partners are Shopify-only at this stage)
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: Mixed — pick partners that span the D2C/wholesale axis to validate both flows

where_they_live.primary_channels: Where Manuva sources design partners (not where the tactic lives): Indie Beauty Industry Group AU FB (~5K), AU Coffee Roasters FB groups (~2-3K), AU Candle & Soap Makers FB (~15-20K), r/coffee, r/skincareformulators, LinkedIn (warm intros to founders in target vertical), Craftybase forum exits, Katana defectors posting on G2 and Reddit.
where_they_live.directories_communities: Common Paper design-partner template repository (commonpaper.com), SaaStr design-partner playbook posts, OpenView's vertical-SaaS resources, Tidemark VSKP (Vertical SaaS Knowledge Project), Y Combinator design-partner essays.
where_they_live.industry_facebook_group_size: Source pool: ~50,000 total members across AU indie-maker FB groups Manuva can mine for design partners
where_they_live.podcasts_voices: Lenny Rachitsky (product/design-partner episodes), This Week in Startups, SaaStr (Jason Lemkin on early customers), Tidemark Vertical SaaS Knowledge Project podcast, Dave Yuan interviews
where_they_live.events_trade_shows: Naturals & Organics Australia, Cosmetics & Personal Care Trade Show (NCIA), Melbourne Coffee Expo, Sydney Coffee Festival — these are where Manuva would meet potential design partners in person. Sponsorship $2-8K range, or attend as a non-sponsor founder for $200-500.
where_they_live.search_keywords: design partner agreement, design partner program SaaS, early customer pilot SaaS, founding customer program, charter customer program

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 4 — founders explicitly looking to influence tooling are responsive to a personal 'I'm building X for brands like yours; want to shape it with 4 others?' DM/email. 5-15% response rate is typical, vs 1-2% for cold sales pitch.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 5 — 'Looking for 5 design partners' LinkedIn post with concrete ICP and offer terms is a viral motion in vertical SaaS. Tom Tunguz / Tidemark / SaaStr have written this playbook many times.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 3 — outsider founder is actually fine here BECAUSE design partner motion is explicitly 'I don't know your industry, teach me'. Reframe outsiderness as a feature: 'Outsider engineer, not yet-another-consultant, who will build exactly what you ask for.'
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Built-in to the motion — every design partner is contractually agreeing to be a case study reference

foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Design partner conversion to paid: industry typical 60-80% (much higher than 14-day free trial). Sample sizes are small but Common Paper / SaaStr report 70%+ conversion when program is well-scoped. For Manuva: target 4 of 5 partners convert.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: RECOMMENDED MANUVA DESIGN-PARTNER PROGRAM: Charter Partner Program. Recruit 5 partners total across 3 verticals (2 cosmetics/skincare, 2 candle/soap/homewares, 1 coffee roaster). 6-month term. Terms: (a) Free Manuva Pro tier for 6 months; (b) 50% off list ($249 Pro pricing) for 24 months post-conversion; (c) bi-weekly 30-min founder call + Slack channel for direct feedback; (d) commit to one written case study + one reference call to prospective customers per quarter; (e) named in launch press as a Charter Partner; (f) priority feature request lane (not exclusivity, but priority); (g) no equity offered — Manuva is bootstrapped and equity at pre-revenue is too speculative for SMB founder. Use Common Paper free template as base. Start recruitment now (months -3 to 0). Goal: 5 signed, 4 converting, 4 case studies by month 9. Reference halo unlocks 15-30 downstream customers by month 12.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 1 (months -3 to 6) — recruit and run before public launch

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Best-practice playbook today is Common Paper's free Design Partner Agreement template — has standardised the contract layer of the tactic. Most successful vertical SaaS (Zenoti, Toast, ServiceTitan, Procore, Vertical SaaS unicorns profiled by Tidemark) ran some version of this motion at $0-$1M ARR. SaaStr / OpenView / Tidemark publish the playbooks.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Most playbooks assume well-funded founder with VC-backed scarcity to dangle. Solo bootstrapped founder must lean harder on 'shape the product' and 'priority roadmap' instead of equity or aggressive discounts. Gap in published playbooks: solo-founder version of design-partner motion at sub-$5K MRR scale.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: Common Paper data: 49% of agreements 3-6mo term, 43% include future discount. SaaStr: 'most under-utilised early-stage motion'. Tidemark: vertical SaaS that does NOT do this loses to peers that do.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: n/a (tactic study; Common Paper template is dominant contract artefact)
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: n/a — design partner motion is contract + cadence + product, not integrations

partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: Industry FB groups + LinkedIn warm intro are the right channels for design partner recruitment, not sponsorships

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 5 design partners signed; 4 convert to paid by month 9. Reference halo: 10-20 additional paying customers by month 12 attributable to design partner case studies and references.
profitability_math.realistic_12mo_mrr_contribution_aud: Direct: ~AU$1,000/mo (4 partners × $249 Growth-equivalent at 50% off). Halo-attributable: AU$2,500-$5,000/mo (10-20 customers × $150-$250 ARPU).
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: Design partner motion is the FOUNDATION of the path to AU$3-5K MRR, not the bulk of revenue. Sequence: months -3 to 0 recruit 5 partners; months 0-6 run program + ship lot tracking + accounting connectors that partners help spec; months 6-9 harvest 4 case studies; months 9-12 use case studies + reference calls to close 15-30 additional vertical customers via founder-led outbound. Compounding effect: $3-5K MRR by month 12 is mostly halo-driven, not partner-driven directly.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: Design partners are catalyst, not bulk. 5 design partners → ~150-300 downstream customers across 24 months gets you to $1M ARR at blended $250-$300 ARPU.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 3 — 5 partners × 6 months × ~8 hours/month = 240 hours of founder time across pilot phase. Demanding but bounded. More than 5 partners and quality drops; fewer than 3 and reference halo is weak.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: Months 9-12 — pilot is unprofitable directly; reference halo turns the unit economics positive by month 9-12
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Initial gross margin is negative-to-near-zero because of founder-time investment. But this is acquisition cost, not COGS — properly accounted as CAC, not gross margin.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 1 — this is the highest-priority tactic for Manuva months -3 to 6. The solo founder's biggest constraint is credibility, and design partners are the cheapest credibility purchase available. Skip this and Manuva loses 12 months.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: RECOMMENDED MANUVA-SPECIFIC TACTIC PARAGRAPH: Run a 5-partner Charter Program across cosmetics (2), candles/soap (2), and coffee (1), each on a 6-month free Pro tier + 50% off 24 months post-conversion, in exchange for case study + reference rights + bi-weekly feedback. Source partners via Indie Beauty Industry Group AU, Craftybase exits, and Katana defection threads on G2. Use Common Paper's free template as the contract base. Avoid equity (premature; signals desperation to AU SMB founders). Cap at 5 partners — beyond that, solo founder cannot maintain quality. Risks: (1) selection risk — picking partners whose feedback skews product toward niche; counter by spreading across 3 verticals; (2) conversion fail — if discounted Pro at $249 is still too expensive at month 6, partners churn and you have nothing; mitigate by getting WTP confirmation in writing during pilot; (3) timeline drift — 6 months can become 12 if scope creeps; commit to a fixed end date and a 'graduation moment' contract clause; (4) IP/feature contamination — use Common Paper template's IP clauses verbatim, do NOT promise partners feature exclusivity (it kills future sales); (5) over-investment in one partner — cap founder hours at 8/month per partner.
